recipes.name: Million Dollar Cabbage Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (3 ounce) packages ramen noodles (without flavor packets), lightly crushed

steps.text: Make the dressing: Whisk oil, sugar, vinegar, and soy sauce together in a bowl until sugar dissolves. Refrigerate until needed.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Spread broken ramen noodles onto a baking sheet with sesame seeds and almonds.
Bake in the preheated oven, stirring often and watching carefully to prevent burning, until lightly browned, about 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool for 5 to 10 minutes.
To serve, mix cabbage, green onions, and toasted ramen mixture together in a salad bowl until thoroughly combined. Add dressing and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Million Dollar Cabbage Salad
raw_recipe.description: This million dollar cabbage salad features crunchy toasted ramen noodles, almonds, and sesame seeds. A great use of Chinese napa cabbage.

review.reviewBody: I have made this salad many times and it is a family favorite. I cut oil down to 1/3 cup and use a 1/3 cup of Balsalmic vinegar. I add chopped garlic, decrease sugar to 1/4 cup and add 5-6 packets of splenda. This salad can also be made with Romaine lettuce and cranberries instead of cabbage for a little holiday flare.

My whole family loves it! Here are my modifications: I cut the sugar in 1/2. My kids are not fans of onion so I omit them or put them on the side. For a bit more flavor I like a bit of chopped fresh flat leaf parsley and shredded carrot(2T) which makes this salad even more vibrant looking. A tip I'd like to share is to add about 1/2 tsp. sesame oil. This gives a wonderful flavor. The dressing will emulsify and not seperate once it's cold so chill it and whisk again before pouring on. I like to pour the dressing about 15 minutes before eating or the ramen is too crunchy for me! :)
I've added chunk cooked chicken breasts, Pinneapple and sometimes mandarin oranges

I emulsified the dressing so that it wouldn't separate overnight as I knew I'd be using the leftover dressing. Otherwise I followed the directions as written, only I keep the crunchy bits as a topping at the last minute instead of mixing in as we can't eat the whole salad in one sitting. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

Yummy, easy salad! I subbed a little sesame oil in place of a small amount of the vegetable oil, and it was delicious. Definitely keep an eye on the noodles and almonds while you’re toasting them, as mine was getting overly browned at around 7 minutes.
I make this quite often. Recipe calls for WAAAY too many sesame seeds! All that’s needed is 1-2 tablespoons! I always add a can of mandarin oranges (drained) & about a half cup of chopped cilantro.

I got this very same recipe several years ago and nearly every time I make it someone requests the recipe. This is great stuff! I make ahead of time and store all three parts separately (nappa, ramen noodle mix, and sauce). Transport to family meal and assemble just before serving.

We LOVE this recipe. I have made it many times (the kids keep requesting it). I have busy teenagers in the house and sending out a text stating I have made million dollar salad sends them home for dinner. I make it just as is except for doubling the ramen noodles. I often make it with crispy orange beef (from this site)and vegetable fried rice. Delicious!
when l make this we put the ramen noodles on top just before serving so they don't get soft. can also add a little red cabbage for more color and some grated carrot. yummy
Good salad, a little sweet for my taste though. I will definitely try it again, but will modify the amount of sugar.

I have been making a version of this for years. Lots of good recommendations on here to add to it or sub Splenda for the sugar. I've always made mine with broccoli slaw and used the flavor packets instead of soy sauce. Adding a little sesame oil is also a great idea. You will be surprised by how tasty this is!
Cold salad
I love this!!! It’s time to say this recipe is amazing and a people pleaser!
This was absolutely delicious! LOVED IT!
Don't change a thing!
The recipe I've always used includes the seasoning packet that comes with the Ramen Noodles, in the dressing.
I've made this exact recipe for many years. It's always a hit! Delicious!
This salad so super easy and the dressing was the star!!
My 85-year-old mom has been making this for decades, she adds chicken. It was always my favorite!

I have been making this salad since the mid 90s, but I make the dressing with seasoned rice vinegar and add a tsp of powdered ginger. I also add shredded chicken and sliced almonds and toast the sesame seeds. For ease, use shredded coleslaw mix.
